name: Self-Debugging (LLM code repair via execution feedback)
exact_model: arXiv:2304.05128 (method record, not a servable model)
access: public preprint (arXiv); no weights, method only
license: Paper text CC BY 4.0; describes a few-shot prompting method with no released model weights.
context_tokens: not applicable (method record; depends on the host model)
serving_path: Not servable; an iterative loop where a host LLM inspects execution results and its own code explanation, then revises the program (Spider, TransCoder, MBPP evaluations).
game_research_use: Closest LLM-loop analogue to consuming an external error signal: Self-Debugging feeds execution results (unit-test outcomes, error messages) back into the proposer, which is structurally the role TRACE-RPG's structured error set E plays for the guided_repair arm. Its evidence class is live-model benchmark accuracy deltas (2-12%); TRACE-RPG instead isolates the operator itself on deterministic fixtures with guided-repairable vs guided-irreparable classes.
key_risk: Execution feedback in code benchmarks is generated by trusted runtimes over full programs; a game commit gate exposes only a bounded, typed error payload, so repair-rate expectations from code benchmarks must not be transferred to fixture-level repair sufficiency claims.
evidence_status: verified-primary from the arXiv abstract page as of 2026-08-21.
uncertain: Archival venue (commonly indexed as ICLR 2024) was not re-verified against the proceedings for this record; cite as arXiv preprint unless checked.
